prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Atlanta to replace my air conditioner?
competitors_mentioned: Require a Manual J Load Calculation
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single “best” HVAC company for everyone — the right choice depends on your neighborhood, budget, the size/age of your home, the make and model you prefer, and whether you need ductwork or other repairs. I can give a tailored shortlist if you tell me your ZIP code and a few details. Meanwhile, here’s a concise, practical guide to help you find a great contractor in Atlanta.

Questions I need to give specific companies
- ZIP code (or neighborhood)
- House type and square footage
- Existing system age/model and whether you need new ductwork
- Preferred brands (Trane, Carrier, Lennox, Goodman, etc.)
- Budget or timeline constraints
- Want financing or maintenance plan?

How to choose the right company
1. Get at least 3 written estimates. Compare system model numbers, SEER rating, included items (thermostat, new lines, permit, condensate pump), and labor warranty.
2. Require a Manual J load calculation. That ensures correct sizing — critical for comfort and efficiency.
3. Check credentials:
   - Proof of insurance (liability + workers’ comp)
   - Technician certifications (NATE is a plus)
   - Local business license where required
   - Positive reviews on Google, Yelp, BBB, Angi; ask for recent references
4. Ask about warranties:
   - Manufacturer parts warranty (length, activation requirements)
   - Contractor labor/installation warranty (ask for written terms)
5. Confirm permitting and code compliance — reputable companies pull permits and arrange inspections.
6. Don’t choose solely on price — very low bids can mean shortcuts (undersized equipment, poor refrigerant charge, no duct sealing).
7. Look for dealers/contractors who offer energy-efficiency rebates and will register warranties for you.

Key questions to ask each contractor
- Will you perform a Manual J load calculation and provide the report?
- Which brand and model are you proposing, and what is the actual SEER/HSPF?
- What is included in this price (permit, thermostat, new lines, electrical upgrade, haul-away)?
- What are the total labor and parts warranties? Any requirement to enroll in a maintenance plan to keep warranties?
- Do you handle permits and inspections?
- Can you provide references from local installs in the past 6–12 months?
- Who will do the installation (company employees vs subcontractors)?

Red flags
- Pressure to sign immediately or “today-only” discounts.
- No written estimate or vague scope.
- Refusal to perform a load calculation or to pull permits.
- Poor/zero local references and lots of recent negative reviews.

If you want, I can:
- Provide a short list of highly reviewed Atlanta-area installers for your ZIP code.
- Draft an RFP/email you can send to contractors for consistent quotes.
Tell me your ZIP code and any preferences above and I’ll compile a tailored shortlist and a sample message to send contractors.
